doc_screened_files.reason: The query stack enters `is_const_evaluatable` immediately before the CTFE call, so this is the most direct place where the invalid const-generic default should be rejected instead of being evaluated.

The stack goes through `FulfillmentProcessor::progress_changed_obligations` before the const-evaluatable query, so overly permissive obligation processing here could let an already-bad constant keep flowing into evaluation.
`FnCtxt::select_all_obligations_or_error` is on the stack right before well-formedness checks finish, making it a likely place where the earlier E0381 on `s` was not converted into a hard stop.
The failure happens while `check_item_well_formed` is running, and this file owns that pass; if it fails to short-circuit on the uninitialized-local error, CTFE can still be triggered.

This is the type-checking phase coordinator that drives well-formedness and obligation checking, so it sits at the control boundary where an invalid const-generic default should be blocked before later queries run.
The ICE is reached through `eval_to_allocation_raw_provider` and `eval_to_const_value_raw_provider`, so this query layer is the direct bridge from type checking into the failing interpreter path.

`InferCtxt::const_eval_resolve` appears in the stack between trait selection and const evaluation, so this is a plausible handoff point where an error should be propagated instead of continuing with invalid input.

This is the exact panic site reporting that the type checker should prevent reading from a never-written local, so it is the immediate symptom location and likely where the invariant is being observed.
Const generic defaults are part of item type collection, and this file computes item types and const-related metadata that later well-formedness and const-evaluatable checks consume.
The failing code uses a const generic default, so the generic-argument validation path that builds and checks defaults is a plausible upstream source of the bad constant reaching CTFE.
